AttrHelp.DEX: Dexterity — saves that need poise, speed or reflexes: dodging, climbing, sneaking, balancing. Acting in the first round of combat and running from danger both take a DEX save. At 0 DEX you are paralyzed.

AttrHelp.WIL: Willpower — saves to persuade, deceive, interrogate, intimidate, charm, provoke, or manipulate spells. A spell cast while deprived or in danger may call for a WIL save. At 0 WIL you are delirious.

ActionRule.cast: Hold the spellbook in both hands, read it aloud, then add a Fatigue. Deprived or in danger, the Warden may ask for a WIL save.
ActionRule.disarm: Deal with a trap you have found. Searching usually finds traps; the Warden resolves the rest.
ActionRule.dodge: Get clear of a springing trap — usually a DEX save. Trap damage comes off STR or DEX, not HP.
ActionRule.force: Force a locked, stuck or blocked door — or wedge it shut — with tools or raw strength. Loud actions may draw an encounter.
ActionRule.hurry: Spend the action moving up to 120 ft instead of 40 ft. Moving quickly risks a Dungeon Events roll.
ActionRule.listen: Listen, smell or watch at a door or wall for signs of life and other hazards beyond it.
ActionRule.panic: Make a WIL save to overcome panic. On a success the condition ends.
ActionRule.rest: Restore all HP. Needs a light and a safe place, and danger makes it impossible. It does not remove Fatigue.
ActionRule.search: Search one object or location exhaustively: it reveals hidden treasure, traps and secret doors. A large room may take a few turns.

CAIRN.Dungeon.Help:
Dungeon exploration, turn by turn.
1. The Warden describes; each player declares a movement and one action — the list button on your row offers them.
2. The Warden resolves everyone's actions at once.
3. Record what was used; the Warden may roll a Dungeon Event.
A turn is about 40 ft and one action, or the action spent to move up to 120 ft. Moved too far? The undo beside the distance takes the token back to where the turn began.
Click for the Rules Summary.

Critical.Label: Critical Damage
Critical.Text: Damage past 0 HP comes off STR, then a STR save at the new score. A PC that fails can only crawl, and dies within the hour if left untreated.

Deprived.Label: Deprived
Deprived.Text: A PC lacking a crucial need is Deprived: they cannot recover HP, Attributes or item slots, and each day Deprived adds a Fatigue.

Detachment.Label: Detachment
Detachment.Text: A large group fighting as one. Attacks against it by individuals are impaired; its own attacks are enhanced and deal blast damage.

Enhanced.Label: Enhanced
Enhanced.Text: Fighting from a position of advantage: roll 1d12 damage instead of the normal die.

Fatigue.Label: Fatigue
Fatigue.Text: Each Fatigue occupies one slot and lasts until the PC can recuperate — a full night's rest in a safe spot.

Impaired.Label: Impaired
Impaired.Text: Fighting from a position of weakness: roll 1d4 damage regardless of the weapon's own die.

Morale.Label: Morale
Morale.Text: Enemies save WIL to avoid fleeing on their first casualty and again at half strength. Morale does not affect PCs.

Panic.Label: Panic
Panic.Text: A panicked character has 0 HP, does not act in the first round of combat, and all of their attacks are impaired. A WIL save as an action shakes it off.

CAIRN.RulesRef.Shared: The rules summary is open on every player's screen.
CAIRN.RulesRef.Title: Rules Summary

Attributes.Title: Attributes
Attributes.Str: Strength (STR) — physical power: lifting gates, bending bars, resisting poison.
Attributes.Dex: Dexterity (DEX) — poise, speed and reflexes: dodging, climbing, sneaking, balancing.
Attributes.Wil: Willpower (WIL) — persuading, deceiving, interrogating, intimidating, charming, provoking, manipulating spells.
Attributes.Outside: Damage taken outside of combat goes to an Attribute instead, usually STR.
Attributes.Zero: At 0 STR a PC dies, at 0 DEX they are paralyzed, and at 0 WIL they are delirious.

Saves.Title: Saves
Saves.Roll: Roll a d20 against the Attribute: equal to or under succeeds, above fails. A 1 always succeeds and a 20 always fails.
Saves.When: A save avoids the bad outcome of a risky choice.
Saves.Contest: When two opponents each try to overcome the other, whoever is most at risk saves.
Saves.Together: When characters act together, whoever is most at risk saves — usually the lowest relevant Attribute.

Hp.Title: Hit Protection
Hp.What: HP is the ability to avoid damage in combat, not health or fortitude, and it is never lost for long.
Hp.Scars: An attack that takes a PC to exactly 0 HP is looked up on the Scars table, by the HP lost in that attack.

Healing.Title: Healing & Recovery
Healing.Hp: A few moments' rest and a drink of water restore lost HP, but may leave the party exposed.
Healing.Bandages: Bandages stabilize a character who has taken critical damage.
Healing.Attributes: Attribute loss is usually restored with a week's rest, helped by a healer or other expert.

Inventory.Title: Inventory
Inventory.Slots: Ten slots, but only four or five items carried comfortably without bags, mounts or carts. A Backpack holds up to six slots of items or Fatigue.
Inventory.Size: Most items take one slot. Petty items take none, bulky items take two. Coin under 100gp is petty.
Inventory.Full: A full inventory — all ten slots — reduces a PC to 0 HP. No one can fill more than ten.

Fatigue.Title: Deprivation & Fatigue
Fatigue.Deprived: A PC lacking a crucial need, such as food or rest, is Deprived and cannot recover HP, Attributes or Fatigue.
Fatigue.Days: Deprived for more than a day: add a Fatigue for each day.
Fatigue.Fatigue: Casting spells and events in the fiction also add Fatigue. Each takes one slot until the PC can recuperate, such as with a full night's rest in a safe spot.
Fatigue.NoRoom: No free slot for a Fatigue: drop an item.

Panic.Title: Panic
Panic.When: Surrounded by enemies, enveloped by darkness or facing their greatest fears, a character saves WIL or becomes panicked. Having no light source can do it too.
Panic.Effect: A panicked character has 0 HP, does not act in the first round of combat, and all their attacks are impaired. A WIL save as their action overcomes it.

Combat.Title: Combat
Combat.Round: A round is about ten seconds. PCs act first, then their opponents; each side's actions happen simultaneously.
Combat.First: In the first round, each PC must pass a DEX save to act, or loses their turn.
Combat.Turn: On their turn a character moves up to 40ft and takes one action. Actions are declared before dice are rolled; something risky calls for a save.
Combat.Hit: Attacks always hit: roll the weapon die, subtract the target's Armor, and deal the rest to HP.
Combat.Many: Several attackers on one foe roll every die and keep the single highest. Two weapons at once: roll both, keep the highest.
Combat.Modifiers: Impaired attacks (weakness, cover, bound hands, very distant targets) and unarmed attacks roll d4. Enhanced attacks (advantage, a helpless foe) roll d12.
Combat.Blast: Blast attacks hit every target in the area, rolled separately for each.
Combat.Critical: Damage past 0 HP comes off STR, then a STR save at the new score to avoid Critical Damage. A PC who fails can only crawl, and dies within the hour unless stabilized.
Combat.Retreat: Retreat always takes a DEX save and a safe place to run to.

Armor.Title: Armor
Armor.Subtract: Subtract Armor from every damage roll before it reaches HP.
Armor.Cap: Shields and similar give their bonus (+1 Armor) only while held or worn. Nothing can have more than 3 Armor.

Magic.Title: Magic
Magic.Spellbook: A Spellbook holds one spell and takes one slot.
Magic.Cast: Anyone can cast by holding a Spellbook in both hands and reading it aloud, then adding a Fatigue.
Magic.Enhance: Given time and safety, a spell can be enhanced — more targets, more power — at no extra cost.
Magic.Danger: Deprived or in danger, the caster may have to save WIL. Failure costs on par with the intended effect: Fatigue, the book, injury, even death.
Magic.Scrolls: Scrolls are petty, cause no Fatigue, and vanish after one use.
Magic.Relics: Relics cause no Fatigue, have limited uses, and a recharge condition.

Dungeon.Title: Dungeon Exploration
Dungeon.Turn: On their turn a character moves about 40ft and takes one action, or spends the action to move up to three times as far — which risks a Dungeon Events roll.
Dungeon.Actions: Actions are any non-passive activity: searching, forcing doors, listening, disarming traps, fighting, casting, resting. Loud ones may draw an encounter, and some take several turns.
Dungeon.Search: An exhaustive search of one object or location takes a turn and reveals hidden treasure, traps or secret doors.
Dungeon.Rest: Resting a turn restores all HP, but needs light and a safe location, and does not remove Fatigue.

Reactions.Title: Reactions
Reactions.Lead: When an NPC's reaction is not obvious, roll 2d6:

Morale.Title: Morale
Morale.Save: Enemies save WIL to avoid fleeing at their first casualty and again at half their number. Groups may use their leader's WIL; lone foes save at 0 HP.

Fate.Title: Die of Fate
Fate.Roll: Roll 1d6 when an outcome is uncertain: 4 or more generally favours the PCs, 3 or under usually means bad luck.

CAIRN.Scar.Deferred: The gain waits — take it from the Growth tab when the fiction allows.
CAIRN.Scar.Lead: Damage took this character to exactly 0 HP.
CAIRN.Scar.LeadPick: Choose the row of the Scars table this character takes.
CAIRN.Scar.NoChange: Nothing changed — the roll did not beat what they had.
CAIRN.Scar.NoTable: The Scars table is missing from the tables compendium.
CAIRN.Scar.Notice: {name} has a Scar to roll — {lost} HP lost.
CAIRN.Scar.Resolve: Roll the gain this Scar still owes
CAIRN.Scar.Title: Scars

FollowsClock.Name: Follows the clock
FollowsClock.Hint: While this is the active scene, its darkness follows the world time: dark from 20:00 to 04:00, light from 06:30 to 17:30, with dawn and dusk between. Leave it off for dungeons and interiors.

CAIRN.ScrollHint: A Scroll is petty, causes no Fatigue, and is consumed after a single use.
CAIRN.SetAside: Set aside — it stays written down and leaves your hands

ActionMacros.Name: Actions menu macros
ActionMacros.Label: Choose macros
ActionMacros.Hint: Drop Macros here from the directory or a compendium. Every character's Actions menu lists them, each run with that character as its actor; a player sees only the ones they may run.
ActionMacros.OnlyMacros: Only a Macro can go here.
ActionMacros.Empty: No macros yet. Drop one here.

BestiaryArt.Name: Bestiary artwork
BestiaryArt.Hint: Lay the images in the artwork folder over the Bestiary compendium — portraits/ on the portrait, tokens/ on the token — on every world load and for every player. One file per monster, named after it (Blink-Dog.webp). The compendium itself is never changed; turning this off brings the core icons back.

BestiaryArtPath.Name: Bestiary artwork folder
BestiaryArtPath.Hint: A folder under Data/ holding portraits/ and tokens/. Default: cairn2e-assets.

ClockDarkness.Name: Scene darkness follows the clock
ClockDarkness.Hint: A scene with “Follows the clock” ticked in its Environment settings grows dark at dusk and light at dawn while it is the active scene. Turn this off if a lighting module already does it, or the two will overwrite each other.

Animations.Name: Cairn animations for Automated Animations
Animations.Hint: Replace the Automatic Recognition menu, once, with Cairn's weapons, monster attacks and spells, animated by JB2A Patreon and sounded by PSFX. A later version only adds its new entries: an entry you edit or delete stays that way. Turning this off stops any further changes; what is already in the menu stays.

CAIRN.SlotCostLocked: A Scroll is petty by rule: it takes up no slots.
CAIRN.SpellbookHint: Cast by holding it in both hands and reading aloud; then add a Fatigue.

CAIRN.Store.BuyRateHint: A percentage of each item's cost. 100 is the price in the book; above it the store is dear, below it there is a sale on.
CAIRN.Store.CartEmpty: Drag things here, or press + on a row.
CAIRN.Store.CoinSetAside: No room for the coin where it was going — {amount} gold pieces were set aside, on your Aside tab.
CAIRN.Store.DeleteConfirm: Delete {name}? Its shelves are forgotten; the items themselves are untouched.
CAIRN.Store.DropHint: Drag items — or a whole folder of them — from a compendium or the Items directory onto the shelves.
CAIRN.Store.FolderAdded: {count} items from {folder} are on the shelves.
CAIRN.Store.FolderEmpty: Nothing in that folder is for sale.
CAIRN.Store.FolderNothingNew: Everything in {folder} is already on the shelves.
CAIRN.Store.FolderNotItems: Only a folder of items can be put on the shelves.
CAIRN.Store.NeedsContainer: The coin will not fit on you — you will be asked which container takes it.
CAIRN.Store.NoCharacter: You have no character to shop with.
CAIRN.Store.NoLongerSellable: Something in the sell cart can no longer be sold — a container with something in it now, or a thing that is gone. It was taken out of the cart: check the total and check out again.
CAIRN.Store.NoRoom: That would not fit in your ten slots.
CAIRN.Store.NoneOpen: No store is open to visit right now.
CAIRN.Store.NotSellable: Only gear from a compendium or the Items directory can be put up for sale.
CAIRN.Store.NothingToSell: Nothing of yours has a price.
CAIRN.Store.Pushed: The store is open on every player's screen.
CAIRN.Store.RestoreKept: Items themselves are untouched, and so is everything the characters have already bought.
CAIRN.Store.RestoreLost: Every store you made, and every change to the system's stores — their shelves, names and rates — is lost. This cannot be undone.
CAIRN.Store.RestoreWardenOnly: Only the Warden can restore the stores.
CAIRN.Store.RestoreWhat: This replaces every store in this world with the system's own ten.
CAIRN.Store.SellRateHint: The share of an item's cost this store pays when a character sells it. The SRD prices what is bought and says nothing about selling.
CAIRN.Store.VisitHint: Visit a store the Warden has opened
CAIRN.Store.VisitableOff: Players cannot visit this store. Only Open to players shows it to them.
CAIRN.Store.VisitableOn: Players can visit this store from their character sheet.
CAIRN.Store.VisitableHint: When on, players open this store whenever they like from the Stores button on their character sheet, and can move between every store that is on. When off, they see it only when you use Open to players. Moving to another store empties their cart.
CAIRN.Store.Title: Store

CAIRN.TakeBack: Take back — it returns to your inventory
CAIRN.TakesSlotsHint: You haul it — a bag on your back, a cart pulled with both hands — so it costs slots like anything else. Off, it hauls itself, costs none, and is always on your Aside tab.

CAIRN.Unknown.Hint: Its holder does not know what this is. They see the name, picture and appearance written here, never the real ones, its die, armour, charges or Recharge, and they cannot use it: they can only carry it, set it aside, stow it or hand it over. Reveal it with the eye in the title bar.
CAIRN.Unknown.Name: Unknown item
CAIRN.Unknown.Refused: {name} is a mystery to you. Tell the Warden what you try with it.
CAIRN.Unknown.ToHolderHint: Its holder sees only the name, picture and appearance you wrote for it.

CAIRN.Whisper.Title: Whisper
CAIRN.Whisper.Hint: Only the people picked will see it. Ctrl+Enter sends.
